what_its_for: Valsartan is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension), heart failure, and to protect your heart after a heart attack. Lowering blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It works by relaxing your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard.
how_to_take: Take valsartan by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablets unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and how you respond to the medicine. Common starting doses range from 40 mg to 160 mg once or twice daily. Do not change your dose on your own. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store valsartan at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using salt substitutes or potassium supplements unless your doctor approves, because valsartan can raise potassium levels in your blood. Limit alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Avoid getting up too quickly from sitting or lying down, especially when you first start taking this medicine, as you may feel dizzy. Tell your doctor or dentist about all medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements, especially ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve), as these can reduce valsartan's effectiveness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction); severe dizziness or fainting; little or no urination; muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat (possible signs of high potassium); chest pain; or signs of kidney problems such as swelling in your legs or feet. Also call your doctor if you become pregnant while taking this medicine, as valsartan can harm an unborn baby.
when_it_works: Valsartan starts lowering your blood pressure within a few hours of your first dose. However, it may take 2 to 4 weeks to see the full benefit. Even if you feel well, keep taking the medicine as prescribed. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take valsartan if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can seriously harm or even cause the death of an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control while taking this medicine and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if valsartan passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure. Rise slowly from sitting or lying positions to reduce the risk of falling. Children: Valsartan can be used in children 6 years and older for high blood pressure. The dose is based on the child's weight and will be determined by the doctor. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
